title: Point the web GUI e2e-lane note at the bundles the web scaffold boots today

source.anchor: boots the real web composition from the shipped `apps/cli/config/base.cordis.yml` plus `apps/cli/config/web.cordis.yml`

task:
Problem: .agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-07-24-web-gui-browser-e2e-lane.md:19 states in present tense that `launchWebScaffold()` "boots the real web composition from the shipped `apps/cli/config/base.cordis.yml` plus `apps/cli/config/web.cordis.yml` through the vendored Loader's include mechanism", and line 71 repeats that the in-process scaffold "already loads the same `apps/cli/config/base.cordis.yml` plus `apps/cli/config/web.cordis.yml`"; the .zh.md counterpart carries both sentences at the same lines. `apps/cli/config/` holds only `agent-presets/` today; the shared rows live in packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml and the web surface's rows in packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml, the `dsh --profile` patch-layer bundles that packages/bundle/README.md documents. `launchWebScaffold` is still the scaffold the lane uses (`grep -rln launchWebScaffold apps/web/tests` lists its callers), so the note's mechanism is current and only its paths are stale. .agents/notes/README.md:13 requires an implemented note's paths to be kept current with what shipped.

Required: read the scaffold's source (follow the import from one of the apps/web/tests callers) to see which bundles it composes today, then replace the two stale path pairs with the current bundle files, citing packages/bundle/README.md for the include and patch mechanics instead of restating them; update the Chinese counterpart minimally; re-record the pair with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write .agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-07-24-web-gui-browser-e2e-lane.md`.

Constraints: facts only — paths and names — never the decision, its rejected alternatives, or its consequences; do not touch the scaffold, the bundles, other notes, or anything under .agents/notes/archived/; no new Agent Note. The queue's mandatory coverage run names dsh-app-boot, the plugin that applies the bundles the note now cites; it guards that package, not this edit, and passes before and after.
